_comment: Copy for /issues (the 'Why put Labor last' page). Edit text, photos and source links here; the page reads this file at load. An issue with no image shows the grey placeholder with its 'face' caption. proofs[].href of '#' renders a Source link that goes nowhere until a real URL is pasted in. teaser and home_label feed the six cards on the home page. tab_label and tab_order set the City / Country toggle.
title: Why put Labor last
lede: Six reasons we cannot miss this chance to vote Labor out.
help_line: If this is hitting hard: Lifeline 13 11 14 · Beyond Blue 1300 22 4636

groups.label: Devastating farmers
groups.sub: Fines, towers and a Spanish multinational on your land

issues.face: Photo: Mary and Colin at their gate
issues.caption: Mary and Colin, both 80. Fined $814 at their own gate.
issues.title: Labor is devastating Aussie farmers
issues.body: Mary and Colin are 80. They stood at their own gate and Labor's agency fined them $814. Twelve farmers have been fined. Then Labor handed VNI West to Iberdrola, a Spanish multinational, to build, own and operate.

proofs.text: Twelve farmers fined by VicGrid for standing on their own land.
VNI West handed to Iberdrola to build, own and operate.

issues.teaser: Twelve farmers fined. VNI West handed to a Spanish multinational.

issues.face: Photo: farmer at a council meeting or inquiry
issues.caption: 534 submissions. 493 from locals and farming families.
issues.title: Labor never listens
issues.body: Buloke, Gannawarra and Northern Grampians councils formally oppose VNI West. 534 submissions went to the inquiry, 493 from locals and farming families. Labor removed third-party appeal rights in March 2024. Asked to fix the fines, the Minister said it was "not my remit".

proofs.text: Three councils formally oppose VNI West.
Minister: fixing the fines is "not my remit".

issues.teaser: Three councils and 493 local submissions against it. Appeal rights removed.

issues.face: Photo: farmer alone in a paddock, towers behind
issues.caption: The counselling is paid for by the agency sending the fines.
issues.title: Labor is evil: destroying family farmers and then paying for counselling
issues.body: The farmer mental health program is "funded by VicGrid". That is the same agency sending the fines and the towers. Break them, then pay someone to talk to them about it.

proofs.text: Farmer mental health program "funded by VicGrid".

issues.teaser: The mental health program is funded by the agency sending the fines.

groups.label: Devastating cities
groups.sub: Power bills, groceries and an $11 billion blowout

issues.caption: VNI West: $3.9 billion promised. Up to $11.4 billion now.
issues.title: Labor will bankrupt Victoria
issues.body: A 200% cost increase on VNI West alone. It was $3.9 billion when it was sold to Victorians. It is now $7.6 billion and as much as $11.4 billion. The Western Renewables Link was $479 million in 2019. It is $4 billion now.

proofs.text: VNI West now $7.6 billion to $11.4 billion. ABC, 1 August 2025.
Western Renewables Link: $479 million (2019) to $4 billion.

issues.teaser: VNI West: $3.9 billion promised, up to $11.4 billion now. A 200% blowout.

issues.face: Photo: the Premier at a press conference, or the Gazette notice
issues.caption: Two numbers for the same line: $1.5 billion here, $4 billion in New York.
issues.title: Labor lied about their renewables policies
issues.body: In September the government was still telling Victorians the Western Renewables Link would cost $1.5 billion. Its owner had already told the New York Stock Exchange $4 billion. The Premier ordered a cost review on 15 September that reports after the election. The planning approval was gazetted on 30 September anyway.

proofs.text: Owner's filing to the New York Stock Exchange: $4 billion.
Cost review ordered 15 September, reports after the election.
Planning approval gazetted 30 September. Gazette S554, Amendment GC209.

issues.teaser: $1.5 billion to Victorians. $4 billion to the New York Stock Exchange.

issues.face: Photo: a family at the checkout or reading a power bill
issues.caption: The $275 power bill promise. Still waiting.
issues.title: Labor is pushing up your power bill and your groceries
issues.body: The cost of the transmission lines lands on every power bill in Victoria. The $275 power bill cut Labor promised? Still waiting. And less farmland means dearer food on the shelf.

proofs.text: Transmission costs are recovered through network charges on every bill.

issues.teaser: Transmission costs land on every bill. Less farmland means dearer food.
